title: Anthropic and OpenAI Independently Disprove Exponential Time Hypothesis
summary:
Two leading AI labs have announced that their internal models separately debunked the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), a foundational computer science principle that for decades defined the limits of algorithmic efficiency. While the discovery does not pose an immediate threat to current encryption standards, it introduces uncertainty regarding other security assumptions used to protect internet traffic, potentially impacting how computational difficulty is measured for securing data.

Anthropic reports that its lainternal Claude research model found the key algorithm for a subexponential 3-SAT solution on Oct. 16 using 14M output tokens and no human input. The company later formalized the finding across 1,050 Lean modules, though it noted that the full formalization has not yet been checked by a human. The company also claimed its Claude Opus 5.5 model can rederive the refutation from a short technical sketch, as OpenAI similarly claimed its own models had reached the same conclusion shortly before.

selectedTweets.text:
Holy Moly: One day after OpenAI announced that its model had disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, Anthropic says an internal Claude model independently found a different disproof on the exact same day: October 16.

An internal Claude research model used 14 million output tokens with no human input to discover a subexponential algorithm for 3-SAT.

Anthropic has now formalized the result across 1,050 Lean modules, checked by both Lean and the independent nanoda kernel.

This is more insane: Anthropic says Claude Opus 5.5 can rederive the refutation from just a short technical sketch.

Anthropic's release adds 153,191 lines across 1,063 files,

The paper says no person is yet known to have checked the full formalization.
